subject.title: feat(cli): improve editor handoffs for agents and humans

question: Should crabbox open publish crabbox/editor-handoff/v1 as a supported long-lived automation contract with these fields and foreground child-process semantics?
rationale: The implementation creates a versioned public interface that agents may depend on, so accepting its initial schema and compatibility expectations requires intent from the owner of the recently introduced editor-handoff surface.

options.title: Adopt the versioned handshake
options.body: Accept the schema direction after live proof confirms the stdout, stderr, and foreground lifecycle contract.

options.title: Keep the handoff human-only
options.body: Decline the new machine contract and retain the prose-only editor workflow until a broader CLI automation convention is designed.

options.title: Revise the schema first
options.body: Keep the feature but adjust field names or lifecycle semantics before consumers begin depending on version one.

recommendation.title: Adopt the versioned handshake
recommendation.body: Accept the schema direction after live proof confirms the stdout, stderr, and foreground lifecycle contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current editor-handoff abstraction and are best positioned to decide its supported automation surface.
